sentences.text: Tylosaurus rex is a mosasaur species belonging to the subfamily Tylosaurinae.
Across the species, individuals range in length from about 7.7 m to 13.2 m.
The largest known skull, belonging to specimen KUVP 5033 (“Bunker”), measures up to 1.63 m in length.
Tylosaurus rex is estimated to have reached over 13 m in length and weighed nearly 8.4 t, making it the largest species of the genus.
The mounted T. pembinensis skeleton “Bruce” measures 13.05 m and once held the Guinness World Record for the largest mosasaur on display.
A 5 m long individual bore dermal scales about 3.3 mm across, roughly ninety scales per square inch on its underside.
The elongated, tooth-less rostrum was originally proposed to function as a battering ram for stunning prey or deterring sharks.
Body temperature estimates suggest Tylosaurus was considerably warmer than coexisting cold-blooded fish and sea turtles, and similar to the warm-blooded seabird Ichthyornis.
Specimens of T. proriger reach lengths of 12.8 to 13.7 m, placing them among the largest mosasaurs.
The type locality of Tylosaurus rex is the Wolfe City Formation in Texas, United States.
Tylosaurus rex was formally described in 2026 based on numerous mostly complete fossils from Texas and Kansas that had previously been assigned to T. proriger.
In 1885 Louis Dollo described the genus and species Hainosaurus bernardi based on an almost complete but poorly preserved skeleton from a phosphate quarry in the Ciply Basin of Mesvin, Belgium.
Fossilized cartilage shows that Tylosaurus had a paired bronchi system suggesting two functional lungs, unlike snakes.
The bronchi bifurcation point lies between the first and sixth cervical vertebrae, a position similar to that of whales.
The nasal bones are either free-floating or only lightly articulated to the internarial bar, never fused to each other, making them rare in the fossil record.
The suprastapedial process of the quadrate likely served as the attachment point for muscles that opened the lower jaw.
Skeletochronology of two juvenile humeri indicated ages of 14 and 7 years at death.
Stomach contents show a varied diet of fish, sharks, smaller mosasaurs, plesiosaurs, and non-flying marine birds such as Hesperornis.
Cone-shaped bite marks on a hadrosaur skeleton match the size and shape of Tylosaurus proriger teeth, suggesting scavenging behavior.
Avascular necrosis was identified in every examined North American Tylosaurus skeleton and in the T. bernardi skeleton.
The genus Tylosaurus was established by Marsh in 1872.
Bardet et al. (2006) divided Tylosaurus species into a North American proriger group and a Euro-American ivoensis group based on marginal tooth morphology.
Johan Lindgren first discussed the attribution of H. pembinensis to Hainosaurus in 2005, and a 2010 revision by Bullard and Caldwell transferred it to Tylosaurus as T. pembinensis.
Tylosaurus rex lived during the Late Cretaceous Campanian age.
The genus Tylosaurus lived from about 92 to 66 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
The exact stratigraphic position of the T. rex holotype is uncertain, but its locality indicates it came from the Wolfe City Formation.
Researchers suggest that Tylosaurus had an endothermic metabolism, which is unusual for squamates.
Some authors continue to argue for maintaining Hainosaurus as a distinct genus, citing dental traits not addressed in the 2016 revision.
